newsitem.title: FRANCE: Hefty local back-up to Jan 30 French rail strike.
newsitem.headline: Hefty local back-up to Jan 30 French rail strike.

text.p: A French rail strike called by the CGT and CFDT unions from Wednesday to Friday morning has been backed up with a hefty number of strike notices at local and regional level, according to union information on Tuesday.
The Communist-led CGT union said in a statement its national strike call had been followed up with 289 strike notices by CGT unions at local level, out of about 400 local level CGT unions.
This was on top of the strike notice at national level and not all CGT unions at local level have to issue separate strike notices, a CGT spokesman said.
The statement said strike notices had also been served by 15 CGT union groupings at regional level, and that in 11 cases, the notice was issued jointly with the Socialist CFDT.

CFDT spokesman Bruno Dalberto told Reuters more precise information was not yet available from the CFDT but that the response to the strike call was generally stronger in any case when it was a case of a joint strike call.
In some cases strike notice would be served separately, so the 11 regions where joint notice was served was not necessarily a reliable measure of the CFDT union response, he added.
The SNCF was due to issue preliminary forecasts later on Tuesday on the impact of the strike, which is slated to start at 1900 GMT on Wednesday and run to 0700 GMT on Friday morning.
The CGT is the largest rail union with more than 40 percent of the 180,000 SNCF state railways staff, while the CFDT is second. Their strike call has been joined by the small SUD-Rail union.
The CGT and CFDT called the strike last week to protest against a bill which would create a new company to take over 134.2 billion francs of the SNCF's 208 billion francs in debts.
The new state holding company would become owner of the rail infrastructure and charge the SNCF, which would be operator and manager of the network, fees for using the infrastructure.
The unions argue that the bill endangers the SNCF's rail monopoly amid deregulation pressure at European Union level and says this in turn threatens jobs and the SNCF's public service mandate.
